latest_nl_proof: Assume that g is nonincreasing on [a,b) in the stated sense. By definition, this means that for all real numbers x and y satisfying a <= x <= y < b, we have g(y) <= g(x). The conclusion of the lemma is exactly the same statement. Therefore, for any real x,y with a <= x <= y < b, one has g(y) <= g(x).
role_in_parent: Converts a monotonicity statement on an interval into the desired endpoint comparison.
statement_nl: Let g : R -> R be a function and let a < b be real numbers. If g is nonincreasing on [a,b) in the sense that for all real x,y with a <= x <= y < b one has g(y) <= g(x), then for any real x,y with a <= x <= y < b one has g(y) <= g(x).

domain_restrictions: x is between a and y inclusive: a <= x
x is not greater than y: x <= y
y is strictly less than b: y < b
x and y are real numbers
g is defined on all real numbers
